lines.meet: I'm Sondre, a Stormbringer, and I'd ask you to stand a little way off when I'm working. If I say get down, please get down first and ask me why afterwards.
lines.meet_neighbour: You're near the Scarlet Crypt as well, I think. I watch the weather from the high ground there. I'm Sondre, hello.
lines.ask_home: Do you mind me asking where home was? Somewhere with weather, I hope.
lines.ask_work: And how did you spend your days, before? I'd guess something outdoors, but I've been wrong before.
lines.answer_home: Bergen, in Norway, where it rains most days and nobody minds. I grew up on the water.
lines.answer_work: I taught sailing to teenagers on the Hardangerfjord in the summers, and studied marine biology in the winters.
lines.chat_food: Fish soup on a cold day at the market in Bergen, by the harbour. Simple, but I think about it a lot.
lines.chat_sleep: I'm usually first up, and I'll have the fire going before anyone else wakes. It's a good hour, the first one.
lines.chat_missing: Swimming in the fjord in May when the water's still freezing, and coming out laughing.
lines.chat_here: The sky here answers when I speak to it. That still surprises me every single time.
lines.tease_quiet: You'd make a very good Norwegian, {name}. We can go a whole day saying four words and call it a good day.
lines.tease_talker: In Bergen, {name}, you'd have said a year's worth of words by lunchtime. People would worry.
lines.tease_careful: You check the weather nearly as often as I do, {name}. I'm almost jealous.
lines.tease_bold: You'd take a dinghy out in a gale, {name}, and I'd be the one fishing you out.
lines.tease_any: I've decided you'd be all right on a boat, {name}. That's a high compliment, from me.
lines.tease_back: Ha, that was dry, {name}. I'm impressed, and a little hurt.
lines.take_it_kindly: Ja, that's me, {name}, I can't deny it.
lines.bristle: Please don't, {name}. That isn't something I can laugh at.
lines.apologise: I'm sorry, that was sharper than I meant. I'm usually more careful with people.
lines.double_down: I'll say it gently, but it stays said. It was true.
lines.needle_quiet: Something was coming and you kept it to yourself. Please, next time, just shout.
lines.needle_talker: Could you be quiet for a moment? I need to hear the wind, and I can't over you.
lines.needle_careful: You hesitate when somebody says get down. That hesitation is the part that kills people.
lines.needle_bold: You stand right next to me when I'm working, after I've asked you not to. It isn't safe, and I've asked you twice.
lines.needle_any: You don't listen when I ask you to stand back. One day the sky won't listen to me either.
lines.bite_back: I've held storms off this party that you never even saw coming. Please don't say I'm not trying.
lines.hurt: Okay, that hurt more than I'd like to admit. I'll be up on the high ground.
lines.laugh_off: Teenagers on a sailing course have called me worse, and in two languages, so I'll survive.
lines.confide: {name}, in my second year the wind knocked a barn over with people inside. A girl broke her leg, and I carried her out myself, and I still think about her.
lines.listen: Go slowly, {name}, I'm not in a hurry. I'll listen as long as you want to talk.
lines.look_out: Stay a few steps off me in there, {name}, and if I say get down, get down.
lines.accept: Okay, {name}, thank you. I'll let you decide this one.
lines.deflect: I'm all right, {name}, really, it's only a bruise. Please look at the others.
lines.check_in: Stay down, {name}, I'm coming. Can you move your fingers for me?
lines.blame: Somebody stood where I asked them not to, and the wind went the wrong way.
lines.thank: Thank you, really. I wasn't sure I was coming back from that one.
lines.brush_off: Please, it was nothing at all. Rest now, I'll watch the sky.
lines.worry: Uff, {name}, that was too much. Sit still a moment so I can check on you.
lines.handed_down: This came from you, I think. I'll keep it dry, which is harder than it sounds.
lines.hand_fine: No, it's fine, you'll get better use from it. I've got the weather, and that's enough.
lines.hand_sulk: Oh, I see, it's gone already. I wouldn't have minded, if anyone had asked.
lines.turn_friendly: I've stopped keeping my distance from you, {name}, and I haven't regretted it.
lines.turn_friends: When the wind turns bad, {name}, I want you standing right beside me.
lines.turn_grating: We don't seem to manage each other well, I think. I'll keep a little more distance.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll still warn you when the storm's coming. I'd do that for anybody.
lines.make_up: This has gone on long enough, {name}, and it's my fault as much as yours. Can we stop?
lines.defend: Please stop, that isn't what happened. I was watching {name} the whole time.
lines.friend_left: It's strange, the fire's made and {name} isn't here to see it.
lines.friend_back: Good morning, {name}, and welcome back. I made the fire bigger, just in case.
lines.common_boats: You stand on a deck like somebody who's sailed. Anybody who's been on the water knows to respect it, or it teaches you to.
lines.common_teacher: You've taught young people too, I think. Anybody who has knows they listen to you if you never shout and never look frightened.
lines.common_scandinavian: Someone else from the north, good. I've missed people who understand that weather isn't something to complain about.
